history.summary: No published source was found documenting a specific 'Saiha Shiva Temple' - its location, founding date and management are all unpublished, and are marked (verify) throughout this record. What is verifiable is the Saiha Hindu community context: Saiha town has a small non-tribal Hindu population (traders, government employees, Bengali families) that maintains shrines such as the Kali Mandir at New Colony Veng, Saiha (796901) - a modern concrete temple whose custodians attribute it to the local Bengali community and devotees, with one travel account placing its origins in the 1940s British colonial period (verify - weakly sourced). A Shiva temple serving this community may exist; nothing about it could be confirmed online. Do not conflate it with the Shiv Mandir at Zarkawt, Aizawl (reportedly established 1980 by the local Hindu community) or the Shiv-Parvati Mandir at Hnahthial, which are different shrines in different districts. The Mara (Lakher) tribe of Saiha was evangelised as part of the Mara mission; the indigenous Mizo population is predominantly Christian.

name: Saiha Shiva Temple
town_description: Saiha (also spelled Siaha) is the headquarters of Saiha district in the far south of Mizoram, the homeland of the Mara (Lakher) tribe, near the Myanmar border. The town is overwhelmingly Christian, with churches dominating the townscape. A small non-tribal Hindu community - traders, government employees and their families, including Bengali families - maintains Hindu shrines in the town; the best documented is the Kali Mandir at New Colony Veng, a modern concrete hilltop temple attributed to the local Bengali community and devotees. Hindu festivals such as Durga Puja and Kali Puja are celebrated by this community, and Mizo locals are also reported to visit the temples.
